summary:
H.R. 8772, the "Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2025," provides appropriations for the Legislative Branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025. 

Title I appropriates funds for the House of Representatives, Joint Committees, Capitol Police, Office of Congressional Workplace Rights, Congressional Budget Office, Architect of the Capitol, Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, Government Accountability Office, and related entities. It includes specific appropriations for intern allowances established under prior acts (e.g., 2 U.S.C. 5322a, 2 U.S.C. 5106, Pub. L. 117-103). Section 110 mandates that unobligated balances in Members' Representational Allowances be deposited into the Treasury for deficit reduction. Section 111 limits vehicle leasing from such allowances to $1,000 per month. Section 112 directs federal entities providing cybersecurity assistance to the House to apply minimization procedures to protect privileged information. Section 113 amends section 303(f) of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (42 U.S.C. 13212(f)) to remove certain long-term lease requirements for the House of Representatives. Section 114 amends section 312(d)(3) of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 1992 (2 U.S.C. 2062(d)(3)) to authorize the use of the child care center revolving fund for telecom expenses. Section 115 amends 5 U.S.C. 4120 to require Capitol Police Board approval for international training. Section 116 prohibits the Architect of the Capitol from paying incentive bonuses to contractors behind schedule or over budget. Section 117 authorizes the Architect of the Capitol to enter into cooperative agreements and plant material exchanges. Section 118 limits the Library of Congress's obligational authority for reimbursable and revolving fund activities to $328,789,000 for FY2025.

Title II contains general provisions. Section 202 restricts fund availability to FY2025 unless expressly provided. Section 209 prohibits the procurement of covered telecommunications equipment (e.g., Huawei, ZTE) using funds under the Act, with phased effective dates (FY2025 for direct procurement, FY2026 for contracting and loan/grant prohibitions) and a one-time, two-year waiver authority. Section 210 exempts the Director of the Government Publishing Office and the Librarian of Congress from statutory pay increase prohibitions. Section 211 amends 5 U.S.C. 13144 to provide that medical or dental care provided by a Member does not constitute a fiduciary relationship. Section 212 prohibits funds for diversity, equity, and inclusion training promoting divisive concepts. Section 213 prohibits discriminatory actions against persons acting on religious beliefs regarding marriage. Section 214 prohibits cost-of-living adjustments for Members of Congress under 2 U.S.C. 4501 for FY2025. Section 215 establishes a spending reduction account with a $0 balance.
